title: Customer-managed network integrity & governance sketch
body:
Purpose:

This is a working sketch for how Redwood Private should treat customer-managed networking from an integrity, approval, and audit perspective. Focus areas: the event model for audit logs, the approval-gate state machine for network handovers and config changes, the ‘evidence bundle’ that travels with approvals, and operator playbook for forensic investigations.

Context / problem we are solving:
- Customers who run Private (VPC / on-prem) need to be able to make network changes on their side without breaking SLAs or producing untraceable changes.
- We need auditable handoffs when customers ask us to run network-affecting operations (e.g., peering, routing changes, port openings for control plane connectivity).
- Security/compliance teams require clear proofs (snapshots, signed digests) that show what changed, who approved it, and what Redwood did in response.

Design goals (high level):
- Minimal friction for customers to self-manage while producing machine-readable evidence for audits.
- Tamper-evident logs and compact evidence bundles that can be archived for retention windows.
- Approval gates that can be automated for low-risk changes and manual for high-risk ones.
- Forensic playbook for SREs and CS to triage incidents quickly.

Event / audit-log model (core fields):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid)
- correlation_id (uuid) 
- actor_id (string, preferably KMS-backed subject)
- actor_type (customer-admin | redwood-operator | system)
- actor_auth (oauth-client-id | cert-fingerprint)
- action (string, e.g., vpc:peering:create, firewall:rule:modify)
- resource (string path, e.g., vpc/12345/route-table/rt-9)
- change_summary (short human string)
- before_digest (sha256 hex)
- after_digest (sha256 hex)
- evidence_refs (list of artifact ids that are part of the bundle)
- request_payload_ref (where to fetch the original payload if > 4KB)
- client_ip
- user_agent
- outcome (accepted | rejected | auto_rolled_back | pending)
- retention_policy (s30d | s1y | s7y)
- signature (base64)

Notes: keep each event small (log line) and attach the heavy artifacts (snapshots, diffs, certs) to an immutable evidence store keyed by event_id. Evidence store entries themselves are referenced via evidence_refs. Evidence items should be sharded and reversible only by audit tooling.

Evidence bundle (what to capture per request/approval):
- config-snapshot-before (text gzipped)
- config-snapshot-after (text gzipped)
- firewall-rules-diff (unified diff)
- routing-table-dump (plain text)
- security-groups-list (plain text)
- control-plane-conn-check (curl + response body)
- operator-notes (free text)
- customer-assertion (signed statement from customer admin; optional but preferred)
- three-way handshake log (if we had to coordinate changes across regions/peers)
- signed-manifest.json listing all evidence item hashes and sizes

Approval gate state machine (sketch):
- requested -> risk-eval (auto) -> if low-risk then auto-approve -> enacted -> verified -> closed
- requested -> risk-eval (auto) -> if medium/high-risk then pending-customer-ack -> pending-redwood-operator -> scheduled-window -> enacted -> verified -> closed
- requested -> emergency -> triage -> operator-override (with 2-person approval) -> enacted -> postmortem-required

Risk heuristics to evaluate automatically (examples):
- Does change touch control-plane connectivity (high)?
- Is the change opening inbound ports from 0.0.0.0/0 (high)?
- Is the change part of a burn-in / high-traffic window (time-of-day)?
- Is the request correlated with a prior failed rollback in last 24h (elevate)?
- Is the actor certified with pubkey / attestation (lower risk)?

Approval UX / API endpoints (high-level):
- POST /private/v1/network-change-requests {manifest, customer_assertion, desired_window} -> returns request_id
- GET /private/v1/network-change-requests/:id/status
- POST /private/v1/network-change-requests/:id/approve {actor_id, signature} -> gate transitions
- POST /private/v1/network-change-requests/:id/evidence/upload (multipart)
- GET /private/v1/evidence/:id -> signed temporary URL (KMS-backed)

Operator playbook - quick triage steps (for SRE/CS):
1) Locate event via correlation_id or request_id.
2) Fetch evidence bundle (signed-manifest, snapshots) and verify hashes.
3) Re-run control-plane connectivity checks from our enrichment agents to reproduce.
4) If mismatch between before/after digests, check for out-of-band changes (customer console).
5) If attack suspected, freeze change-authority and escalate to security.
6) Collect PCAP / console logs for the 5-minute window around the event.
7) Open postmortem ticket and attach evidence bundle.

Forensic queries we should support out of the box:
- Find all events that modified route tables for a given VPC in time range
- List of approval events where actor_type=redwood-operator in past 90 days
- All auto-approved events that later rolled back
- Evidence bundles with signature validation failures

Retention & compliance knobs:
- Default retention for Private customers: 1y for full evidence bundles, 7y for signed-manifests and minimal event lines (configurable per-contract).
- Fast-archive: move compressed evidence to low-cost cold storage after 90 days, with retrieval SLA (48h) for e-discovery requests.
- On-demand export: customer can request a signed export of evidence for a time range (audit export job).

Operational notes & open questions (todo):
- How to handle evidence storage when customer is air-gapped? (Proposal: signed-manifest and small event bundle can be pushed into customer’s S3 endpoint; large artifacts remain on Redwood on request.)
- What signing key infrastructure do we require? HSM-backed keys per customer? Shared Redwood operator key?
- Does retention policy count toward Dedicated storage quotas or is it billed separately?
- Should we auto-mask IPs in artifacts for privacy by default? (Some customers will push for full fidelity.)
- PD-3427: contract clause for evidence retention and export (JIRA).

Action items (next steps):
- Engineering: prototype event schema + evidence store (PRD spike) - assignee: Evan - due 2024-11-22 (JIRA:PD-3501).
- Security: propose signing key model (HSM vs customer-managed) - assignee: Priya - due 2024-11-29 (JIRA:PD-3502).
- Product: finalize approval gate UX and emergency override policy - assignee: Sofia - due 2024-12-06 (JIRA:PD-3503).

Notes to self / collaboration crumbs:
- See Confluence notes under Private-VPC-Onboarding-Playbook for existing handover language.
- Slack thread: #private-deployments (pin: customer-vpc-audit) has customer asks re: long retention.
- Sample evidence size: rough estimate 50–200KB per snapshot, 1–3MB per full bundle for large configs. Budget storage accordingly.

Unresolved: who signs the customer assertion object in multi-tenant dedicated pools? Need legal sign-off on retention windows beyond default.

If this approach looks sound, next doc should be a concrete proto: event schema JSON Schema + simple CLI to bundle evidence and create a request.

End of sketch.
